note: Every capability a composition profile can select, classified shipped (a skill or module owns it) or adopter-supplied (no shipped owner; an adopter builds one satisfying the named contract). The reference-profile validator and the whole-composition completeness check consult this registry through capability-registry-helpers.mjs so a profile that selects an unclassified, unshipped capability is reported as a dangling reference rather than silently accepted. This is a classification record, not a runtime manifest; classify-vs-drift is enforced by validate-capability-registry.ts.

lifecycle-capability.note: Canonical lifecycle capability kinds a workflow profile includes. Open ontology: a profile may split composites, omit optional capabilities, or add its own, so the entries below are the shipped canonical set, not a closed enumeration.

method.note: Named selectable methods, plus an open tail (any other installed skill). A shipped method names its owner skill package; an adopter-supplied method names the contract an installed skill must satisfy.

entries.name: example-mapping
entries.contract: An installed skill providing the example-mapping method as an early-lifecycle Method capability (early-lifecycle-contracts.md), producing a canonical result through the workflow-guide result and provider contracts. No skill-example-mapping ships; the technique appears within bdd-guide but is not owned as a standalone method.

entries.name: user-research
entries.contract: An installed skill providing the user-research method as an early-lifecycle Method capability (early-lifecycle-contracts.md), producing a canonical result through the workflow-guide result and provider contracts. No skill-user-research ships.

entries.name: architecture-review
entries.contract: An installed skill providing the architecture-review method as an early-lifecycle Method capability (early-lifecycle-contracts.md), producing a canonical result through the workflow-guide result and provider contracts. No architecture-review skill ships; skill-adr owns architecture decision records, not the review method.

provider-port.note: A profile selects a whole provider port; the port contract and a self-controlled conformance fake ship, while a real provider adapter is adopter-supplied. The port capability itself is shipped because its contract exists and is conformance-tested.

executor-class.note: Closed vocabulary owned by expectedVocabulary.executorClasses and CI-guarded across declaring sites; the accountable human or external system of record that fills human/external is adopter-supplied.

governance-module.note: A profile selects governance modules by capability, constrained to a classification. The classification vocabulary is shipped; concrete evidence-producing/enforcing/configuration-changing/privileged modules are native to the adopter's harness, CI, and providers.

entries.name: evidence-producing
entries.contract: A native inspection/evaluation module that publishes evidence without applying policy, declared per the module contract (modules.md). The classification and illustrative templates ship; the concrete module is native to the adopter's harness, CI, or providers.

entries.name: enforcing
entries.contract: A native module that can allow, deny, require evidence, or gate at a declared point, declared per the module contract (modules.md). Installation is never enforcement proof; the concrete enforcing hook/gate/admission control is adopter-native.

entries.name: configuration-changing
entries.contract: A native module that mutates durable settings through the configuration provider contract (provider-contracts.md), declared per the module contract (modules.md). The concrete module is native to the adopter's managed-configuration surface.

entries.name: privileged
entries.contract: A native module that can affect protected systems, identities, data, deployment, or organization controls, declared per the module contract (modules.md). The concrete module is native to the adopter's protected systems, identity, deployment, or org-control providers.
